title: Thousands gather in London to express support for Palestinians after three years of ‘genocide’
excerpt:
Twenty arrested in first march since Ed Miliband declared UK’s position was that Israel’s occupation of West Bank was unlawful

Thousands of people have gathered in central London to express their sup...
body_text:
Twenty arrested in first march since Ed Miliband declared UK’s position was that Israel’s occupation of West Bank was unlawful

Thousands of people have gathered in central London to express their support for Palestinians after three years of “genocide” carried out against them by Israel.

The demonstrators, many wearing keffiyehs and holding Palestine flags, gathered on the Embankment at midday on Saturday. Some carried placards reading “End the genocide” and “Free Palestine” as they marched towards parliament. A bride and groom appeared to be among those in attendance and a two-minute silence was held to reflect on the lives lost in Gaza.

The Metropolitan police said 20 arrests had been made, including for criminal damage after demonstrators climbed on to the Battle of Britain memorial, having Palestine Action placards, making a Nazi salute and assaulting police as officers made arrests.

Protesters were calling for the UK government to stop supplying arms to Israel, which various bodies – including the UN, Amnesty International, B’Tselem and Physicians for Human Rights, the latter two of which are Israeli-based – have said is committing genocide against Palestinians in Gaza.

A ceasefire was declared a year ago but Israeli airstrikes have continued in Gaza. In the last year, the overall death toll has risen by a further 1,400 people. Settlers have also ramped up their attacks against Palestinians in the West Bank. According to UN figures, 230 Palestinians were killed in the West Bank by Israeli forces and settlers in 2025.

Husam Zomlot, the Palestinian ambassador to the UK, shared a video from the march on social media. “Three years on, Israel’s atrocities in Gaza and the West Bank continue, and so does the solidarity of the British people. Louder, bigger and not going anywhere. Thank you all,” he said. By Saturday afternoon, organisers said 250,000 people were at the march.

The Met have imposed conditions on the event – which is organised by the Palestine Coalition, which has organised more than 30 mass demonstrations since October 2023, with a counter-protest by Stop The Hate – to “minimise the risk of serious disruption to communities”.

The Met posted on X saying: “The front of the procession has now entered Whitehall where a rally will take place.

“Several arrests have been made so far including a woman and a man with placards declaring support for proscribed organisation Palestine Action.

“We have also arrested a number of protesters on suspicion of criminal damage after they climbed on to the Battle of Britain memorial on Victoria Embankment.”

The national march is the first held since the foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, announced sweeping sanctions on trade with Israeli settlements and declared the UK government would take the official position that Israel’s occupation of the West Bank was unlawful in its entirety. He also told the Commons that settler terrorists supported by Benjamin Netanyahu’s government are committing ethnic cleansing in the West Bank.

At Labour party conference last month, Miliband appeared to reference the marches, which at their peak regularly numbered hundreds and thousands of people, telling the audience in Liverpool: “I want to say to the millions of people in this country and indeed elsewhere who have been moved and outraged by the plight of the Palestinian people: we hear you, you were right.”

Deputy assistant commissioner Carl Galvin said: “We know Saturday’s event, so close to the third anniversary of the terror attack on Israel, has the potential to have a greater impact on communities than the previous national marches.”

Galvin, who is leading the policing operation this weekend, said the force’s presence on Saturday will be “significant”.

“We will also be using powers under the Public Order Act requiring anyone in the protest area wearing face coverings to deliberately conceal their identity to remove them,” Galvin continued.

The Met have imposed conditions on the march and require the group to travel via Westminster Bridge, York Road, Waterloo Bridge and The Strand on to Whitehall, with a rally concluding by 6.30pm. The force has said that any speeches and music must conclude by 5.30pm.

A counter-protest by Stop The Hate is also taking place, with about 30 people gathered outside New Scotland Yard, some with flags.

The force has also imposed conditions on the demonstration “to minimise the risk of serious disruption”. The demonstrators must remain within a designated area outside the Met’s headquarters, with the assembly concluding at 2.30pm.

Last Saturday, on the third anniversary of the 7 October attacks, when Hamas militants broke across the Israeli border to launch a wave of attacks on kibbutzim, border towns, military bases and music festivals, killing at least 1,209 people, a small pro-Palestine student demonstration in central London was held.

The Met publicly appealed to those behind the demonstration to “exercise [their] right to protest on a different date” and admitted that finding the organisers had been “frankly difficult”. In the end, it went ahead and about 100 people attended. Five people were arrested for breaching conditions imposed on the march.

The Palestine Coalition organising the march includes Palestine Solidarity Campaign, Stop the War, CND, the Muslim Association of Britain, Friends of Al Aqsa and the Palestinian Forum in Britain.

title: Eritrea urges UN to intervene in standoff with Ethiopia
excerpt:
Eritrea has asked the United Nations to take “deterrent measures” after what it called Ethiopia’s “declaration of war” in the conflict over the Tigray region.

Eritrea’s request comes a day after Addi...
body_text:
Eritrea has asked the United Nations to take “deterrent measures” after what it called Ethiopia’s “declaration of war” in the conflict over the Tigray region.

Eritrea’s request comes a day after Addis Ababa, in a letter to the Security Council, accused Asmara of launching an “all-out invasion”, saying Eritrean troops had advanced up to 60 kilometres (37 miles) into Ethiopia’s Tigray.

In a separate letter to the council on Saturday, Eritrean Foreign Minister Osman Saleh said the claims of an Eritrean incursion were part of an Ethiopian plan to justify a war of aggression and urged the UN to intervene, invoking Chapter VII of the UN Charter, which allows measures from sanctions to military action.

The neighbouring countries have accused each other of starting a war over Tigray, where Ethiopia says Eritrea is backing rebels.

An alliance of seven armed groups launched attacks against federal Ethiopian forces in the northern region last month, as they attempt to overthrow Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed’s government.

Eritrean forces have since reportedly intruded into Ethiopian territory, with Addis Ababa accusing Asmara of backing the rebel Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF).

The Ethiopian army pushed TPLF rebels back this week and seized the region’s capital, Mekelle. It also said it launched drone strikes against Eritrean troops in the region.

“Eritrea requests the UN Security Council to forcefully condemn Ethiopia’s deplorable declaration of war against Eritrea … and take the requisite deterrent measures,” Eritrea’s Saleh said in the letter on Saturday.

He said Ethiopia’s action would cause “huge devastation to the peoples of both countries and destabilise the whole region”.

Ethiopian Foreign Minister Gedion Timothewos on Friday accused Eritrea of “a blatant act of aggression that engages Ethiopia’s inherent right to self-defence”.

Timothewos invoked Ethiopia’s right to self-defence under Article 51 of the UN Charter, but he did not specify what measures the country was taking.

Faisal Roble, a Horn of Africa specialist, believes both sides are “preparing for the last phase of an open conflict”.

“There is really no doubt that both of them are inching towards an open conflict,” he told Al Jazeera from the Kenyan capital, Nairobi.

“Whatever they write to the United Nations, it is just posturing and making sure that they have some sort of international support on their side,” the analyst added.

In his letter, Saleh called Ethiopia’s actions “deceitful attempts to rationalise its brazen acts of war”, claiming that they were “hollow in substance”.

Eritrean Information Minister Yemane Gebremeskel accused Ethiopia on Friday of pursuing aggression against Eritrea through its demands for sovereign access to the Red Sea. Writing on X, he did not explicitly confirm or deny the reported troop crossings.

Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy reiterated on Monday that Ethiopia must have access to the Red Sea.

Eritrea gained independence from Ethiopia in 1993, and they fought a deadly border war from 1998 to 2000.

Relations improved after Abiy came to power in 2018, but have soured again in recent years.

Landlocked Ethiopia has repeatedly insisted that it has a right to direct sea access, which Eritrea interprets as a threat to invade and seize its port at Assab.

TPLF fighters battled Ethiopian government forces, then backed by Eritrea, in a devastating 2020-2022 war.

title: Socialists set sights on the ground floor of government as GOP warns of bigger plan unfolding
excerpt:
A Fox News segment highlights the growing influence of Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) candidates.

FIRST ON FOX — Dozens of individuals backed by the Democratic Socialists of America are set t...
body_text:
A Fox News segment highlights the growing influence of Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) candidates.

FIRST ON FOX — Dozens of individuals backed by the Democratic Socialists of America are set to appear on ballots as candidates for state legislature seats on Election Day, something Republicans say could set in motion a trend that transforms the Democratic Party.

At least 65 DSA-aligned candidates have advanced to contest state legislative seats in November’s general election. The Republican State Leadership Committee — the official GOP body responsible for ensuring state-level conservative victories — claimed that these races could very well determine the future of the Democratic Party, according to a memo obtained exclusively by Fox News Digital.

"The statehouse trend is also relevant because several prominent DSA-aligned Congressional candidates in 2026 have emerged from state and local political organizing," the memo reads. "These victories demonstrate one potential progression: movement organizations can help develop candidates locally and at the state level, provide them with political experience and organizational networks, and eventually support campaigns for Congress."

SOCIALISTS CHEER ‘SHOCKWAVE’ PRIMARY NIGHT AS DSA-BACKED CANDIDATES WIN, ADVANCE ACROSS THE MAP

Items on a table during an election night party held by the Democratic Socialists of America - LA chapter at The Greyhound on Tuesday, Nov. 4, 2025 in Los Angeles, Calif. (Eric Thayer / Los Angeles Times via Getty Images)

"The scale of that presence matters not only because DSA-aligned candidates could influence the direction of their state legislatures if elected, but because state legislative offices can provide a platform, governing experience, donor networks and organizational infrastructure for future campaigns for higher office," it continues.

The RSLC's methodology included candidates who are DSA members, DSA endorsees or self-identified members of the organization.

DSA-affiliated candidates identified by the RSLC take positions on a number of issues that crucial swing voters and independents may find extreme, including defunding or abolishing police departments, left-wing economic policies and demanding race-based reparations.

Opposition to traditional policing has emerged as a prominent issue among some of the DSA-aligned state legislative candidates identified by Republicans.

"As a State Senator I will continue to do everything I can to end policing and incarceration in New York State," Democratic State Sen. Jabari Brisport’s campaign website reads. Brisport also supports decriminalizing prostitution, arguing that removing criminal penalties for sex workers while maintaining protections against trafficking and exploitation would help keep communities safe.

TALARICO PUT ON DEFENSE AFTER 2020 COMMENTS ABOUT DEFUNDING POLICE RESURFACE: 'WE MUST REPLACE'

Members of the Democratic Socialists of America gather outside of a Trump owned building during a May Day rally in New York City in 2019. (Spencer Platt/Getty Images)

Over in Wisconsin, Democratic State Rep. Ryan Clancy has stood by his statement that police work has "no dignity or value."

"It means that American policing has always been bad and it always will be," Clancy told a local outlet in 2023, alleging that American police forces have their roots in slave patrols. "It’s not like we can get back to this to the early days… American policing… [is] epically racist and classist because that’s a dead end. That is the point of American policing."

Clancy told Fox News Digital that his comments concerned officers who abused their authority over sex workers, although his original remarks and subsequent 2023 interview criticized policing more broadly as an institution he argued was inherently racist and could not be reformed.

He concurred with the RSLC's assertion that DSA-aligned candidates are shaping the future of the Democratic Party.

State Rep. Eleanor Chávez, running with the DSA’s backing in New Mexico, meanwhile has called Immigration and Customs Enforcement "fascist" and compared its agents to the KKK. Republicans in New Mexico have condemned such rhetoric, arguing that it could spur people to commit violence against law enforcement officers.

Despite its propensity to draw attention to its stances on social issues, the DSA bills itself as an economically motivated organization.

NEWSOM ADMITS DEMOCRATIC SOCIALIST IDEAS ‘MAINSTREAM’ IN DEMOCRAT PARTY: ‘PRETTY ALIGNED’

New York City Democratic Socialists hold a rally in Union Square on Nov. 16, 2025, to mark the start of a campaign to tax the rich and win universal childcare. (Selcuk Acar/Anadolu)

To this end, some of its members running for state legislatures have called for reforms some have described as radical.

New York Democratic Assemblywoman Sarahana Shrestha, who is running for re-election with the backing of the DSA, has pushed legislation that would allow the government to acquire the privately held Central Hudson Gas & Electric Corp., potentially through eminent domain if a negotiated purchase cannot be reached.Dylan Wegela, a DSA-backed state house candidate in Michigan, has similarly pushed for state acquisitions of utility companies.

Shrestha agrees with the RSLC's assessment that DSA-aligned state lawmakers could influence the Democratic Party’s trajectory.

"The things DSA-aligned state lawmakers are fighting for are things that are extremely popular with voters, and have been for a long time," she told Fox News Digital. "A majority of our constituents believe the energy sector should not be for profit, healthcare should be single-payer and universal, the government should play a positive role in building necessary infrastructure such as permanently affordable housing and public transit, and so on."

The DSA-affiliated lawmaker also defended her plan to take over the Central Hudson Gas & Electric Corp., citing a feasibility study commissioned by supporters of the bill that found it would lower costs for consumers.

Sometimes, the stances of DSA clash with Democratic policy priorities.

Gabriel Acevero, a DSA-backed lawmaker in Maryland, for instance, opposed a marijuana legalization measure he argued did not go far enough to address racial inequities, declaring that "cannabis legalization without reparations for communities harmed by the intentional drug war is not progressive policy." Scores of DSA-affiliated candidates running in states such as New York, Minnesota and Massachusetts have thrown their support behind reparations for racial minorities.

SOCIALISTS ARE HELPING GOP CAMPAIGNS HEADING INTO NOVEMBER

Republicans have a vested interest in tying the mainstream Democratic Party to the DSA. A Fox News poll from September found that 55% of registered voters had an unfavorable opinion of the DSA.

While some in the Democratic Party argue that Republican attempts to tie the Democratic Party to socialism are bad-faith campaign tricks, party leadership has recently made significant concessions to its left-wing flank.

Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer backed Abdul El-Sayed's more moderate opponent in Michigan's Democratic Senate primary, but a super PAC aligned with Schumer has since committed millions of dollars to supporting El-Sayed's general-election campaign. El-Sayed is a progressive backed by prominent figures on the party's left, but who has said he is not a socialist.

Due to the disorganized nature of the DSA and the varying degrees of affiliation held by candidates, estimates of the number of socialist candidates running for state legislature vary across sources. The Brookings Institution, for instance, found at least 76 had advanced to the general election, while the RSLC’s analysis identified a minimum of 65 running in a total of 24 states.

Though the DSA's gains have received significant attention, a Brookings Institution analysis found that candidates backed by the organization represent only a tiny fraction of the nation's state legislative seats, raising questions about how far the socialist movement's growing influence extends.

"The RSLC has consistently said that socialism starts in the states and that is where we need to stop it," the RSLC’s memo reads. "The DSA’s growing presence in statehouse races could have dangerous impacts for state policy in the short-term, and it reflects a clearly orchestrated long-term effort to build political power from the state-level up."

Every state legislative candidate mentioned was reached for comment by Fox News Digital on Tuesday.

title: 5 marriage mistakes couples make without realizing it — and how to avoid them
excerpt:
Tammy Nelson, PhD, a board-certified sexologist, sex therapist and integrative relationship therapist in Los Angeles, shares five tips for couples to keep their marriages strong over the years.

The s...
body_text:
Tammy Nelson, PhD, a board-certified sexologist, sex therapist and integrative relationship therapist in Los Angeles, shares five tips for couples to keep their marriages strong over the years.

The secret to a happier, longer-lasting marriage may involve much more than chemistry and compatibility.

Recent research published in the journal Family Process found that improvements in communication and emotional safety were linked to greater relationship satisfaction.

Maintaining that connection takes effort, particularly as couples settle into routines and begin to feel as though they already know everything about each other, according to Tammy Nelson, Ph.D., a board-certified sexologist, sex therapist and integrative relationship therapist in Los Angeles.

‘FOOD DIVORCE’ TREND AMONG COUPLES COULD DRIVE THEM APART, EXPERTS WARN

"Compatibility can feel different to different people at different times," she told Fox News Digital. "The relationship will go through developmental stages just like you do."

Recent research published in the journal Family Process found that improvements in communication and emotional safety were linked to greater relationship satisfaction. (iStock)

From losing curiosity to avoiding difficult conversations, Nelson shared five common mistakes that can weaken a couple’s connection — and ways to avoid them.

Losing curiosity about a partner can chip away at attraction over time, according to Nelson.

"That’s how we fall in love, when someone's curious about us," she said. "When they come along and say, 'I'm so interested in you. I'm curious about you.'"

WHY COUPLES SHOULD FLIRT WITH EACH OTHER EVERY DAY — PLUS THE ‘RED FLAG’ TO AVOID

"We're attracted to something in the space in between us — not so much when it's sitting next to us on the couch every night, and so we tend to lose that curiosity."

While someone may feel they know everything about their partner — "what they like to eat, what they'd like to watch on TV, what they might like in bed" — those preferences can evolve over time, Nelson said.

Couples may miss opportunities for connection when they feel affection toward their partner but don't express it, the relationship expert said. (Getty Images)

"Don't put your partner in a box," Nelson said, urging couples to stay curious and ask questions. "Who are they becoming? What are they thinking? What do they desire? What's their vision for the future?"

POLITICAL FIGHTS CAN RIP COUPLES APART — THERAPIST SHARES 3 WAYS TO SAVE A RELATIONSHIP

The therapist suggested that losing curiosity about a partner can sometimes make attention from someone outside the relationship particularly appealing.

"That's why we have affairs, right? Somebody comes along and they're fascinated by us," she said. "We love that. And it's why we pay a therapist, so someone will ask questions about us."

Avoiding difficult conversations — and failing to pay attention to what goes unsaid — can create problems in a relationship, Nelson cautioned.

"Pay attention to what you're not talking about and why," she advised.

Avoiding difficult conversations — and failing to pay attention to what goes unsaid — can create problems in a relationship, the therapist cautioned. (iStock)

When it comes to relationship problems, couples who avoid conflict may be more vulnerable than those who openly disagree.

"It's not the people who fight and communicate all the time — it's the people who aren't fighting, aren't arguing, aren't communicating," the expert said.

COMMON MARRIAGE HABIT COULD QUIETLY KILL YOUR SEX LIFE, EXPERT WARNS

Nelson encouraged couples to notice which topics make them pull back or shut down during conflict — such as money or sex — and instead make an effort to lean into those difficult discussions.

"You're probably avoiding it because you don't want to get into a conflict, which is totally legitimate, but maybe pay attention to those spaces where there could be more room for communicating," she advised.

When couples talk about sex, focusing on complaints rather than what is working can make intimacy more difficult, according to Nelson.

"The key here is not to talk about what's not working or what your partner's not doing, or why you’re not doing it more often," she said.

When couples talk about sex, focusing on complaints rather than what is working can make intimacy more difficult, the expert said. (iStock)

The "magic formula," Nelson said, is for partners to share what they like and what is working.

"The key to the universe is, you get more of what you would appreciate," she said. "If you point out how your partner is not acting the way you want, then you're in conflict, you're defensive, you feel bad about yourself. That's not going to help, it’s not very sexy."

Instead, she recommends focusing on the positive by telling a partner what they've liked about their sex life, whether it is something happening now or a meaningful experience from years ago.

"Whether you’re a new couple or you've been together forever, start with something you appreciate, and then something that you would like more of," she suggested. "Expand on what’s already working."

Another potential mistake is allowing the everyday responsibilities of life to crowd out opportunities for growth and excitement.

Nelson encouraged couples to consider whether their relationship is primarily in "maintenance mode" or "expansion mode."

Maintenance mode involves managing the everyday responsibilities of a shared life, which Nelson said is essential.

"You know, we need to pay the bills. We need to make sure the air conditioner is working," she said. "We need maintenance in a relationship, just like you need maintenance at a job or just in life, but you also need expansion."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Expansion mode, meanwhile, involves trying new things together and finding ways to keep the relationship exciting.

If there’s too much maintenance and not enough expansion, one or both partners could get bored and feel stuck, Nelson cautioned.

"On the other hand, if there’s too much expansion, you're going to feel like you’re always doing something new and there's no rest and maybe not enough connection," she said.

"All relationships need freedom and connection."

Couples may also miss opportunities for connection when they feel affection toward their partner but don't express it, according to Nelson.

She encouraged couples to notice the positive emotions and physical sensations they experience when thinking about their partner — and to share those feelings with each other.

"Where in your heart or in your body are you feeling the most 'juice,' the most 'aliveness,' when you think about your partner?" she asked.

Some people are more aware of these physical sensations than others, Nelson acknowledged.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"But if you can put your hand on your heart or on your stomach or your shoulders and say, ‘you know, when I think about you, I get this warm feeling in my heart’ — that's all you have to share with your partner. And sometimes that means everything to them."

Ultimately, Nelson emphasized that avoiding these common pitfalls comes down to ongoing attention, curiosity and a willingness to keep discovering new things about each other.

Melissa Rudy is senior health editor and a member of the lifestyle team at Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to melissa.rudy@fox.com.

Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

Authorities confirmed multiple people are dead following a shooting in Pennsylvania Friday night, including the suspected gunman, who reportedly died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound.

Police responded to a home just before 5 p.m. local time after witnesses reported seeing a person firing a weapon before entering the house, according to a report from Fox8 Live.

Erie Police Chief Rick Lorah described the scene as the worst he had encountered in nearly three decades in law enforcement, telling local media that investigators were still trying to determine exactly what happened.

"I want to be candid with our community. This is one of the most difficult and heartbreaking scenes our officers and investigators have ever encountered. The loss of life is devastating, and the circumstances we are working through are deeply disturbing," Lorah said, according to Fox8.

Witnesses reportedly told police they saw the shooter run into a nearby home.

POLICE REVEAL NEW DETAILS ABOUT GUNMAN, 5 VICTIMS KILLED IN RURAL MICHIGAN SHOOTING RAMPAGE

Multiple people were killed in a shooting along Perry Street in Erie, Pennsylvania, on Friday, Oct. 9, 2026, authorities reportedly said. (Google Maps)

WFXP reported that the Erie SWAT team and numerous police officers surrounded the home before obtaining a warrant and entering the property.

"It's a horrific scene," Lorah told the station. "There was a large loss of life inside that residence and outside that residence."

Lorah confirmed to WFXP that two women had been killed, but would not confirm the exact number of victims.

"I can tell you that this is a tragic, tragic situation," Lorah said.

MULTIPLE PEOPLE KILLED IN SHOOTING AT IDAHO IN-N-OUT RESTAURANT, SUSPECT DEAD

Erie police responded to the 700 block of Perry Street on Oct. 9, 2026, following reports of a shooting. (Erie Police Department)

Lorah told the station that the suspected shooter was found dead from a self-inflicted gunshot wound.

The city of Erie issued a statement about the shooting, saying the incident resulted in "multiple deaths" and confirming that there was no ongoing threat to the public.

"We understand that this news brings deep shock and sorrow to our residents, and we want to assure the public that the situation has been contained," the city said.

"Our thoughts are with the victims, their loved ones, and everyone impacted by tonight's tragedy," the statement continued. "We will continue working closely with our Erie Police Dept, and will provide updates as soon as verified information becomes available."

Erie police responded to reports of gunfire Friday evening before discovering multiple victims. (Erie Police Department)

Erie police told Fox News Digital that investigators were still processing the crime scene and that Lorah was expected to provide an update Saturday morning.

The department's Criminal Investigations Division continues to investigate the shooting.

This is a developing story. Please check back for updates.

Michael Sinkewicz is a writer for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to michael.sinkewicz@fox.com

title: The storm is here: Georgia-Alabama set to write latest chapter after chaotic week around Hurricane Isaias
excerpt:
Six friends from Los Angeles tell OutKick how a planned trip to Alabama has turned into a six-day sports adventure featuring the Dodgers, Crimson Tide, Falcons and Rams.

TUSCALOOSA, AL — There were t...
body_text:
Six friends from Los Angeles tell OutKick how a planned trip to Alabama has turned into a six-day sports adventure featuring the Dodgers, Crimson Tide, Falcons and Rams.

TUSCALOOSA, AL — There were two sides to the buildup between Georgia versus Alabama heading into tonight's showdown in Tuscaloosa.

First, it was Hurricane Isaias barreling toward the Gulf Coast on Friday afternoon, as evacuations took place and preparations were well underway throughout the Southeast for what was going to be a long night of bad weather.

Second, a massive SEC showdown that will set the tone for both teams moving forward this season, with Alabama hoping to make a statement about where it stands right now during the Kalen DeBoer era, while Kirby Smart hopes to start adding wins against the Tide in regular season play.

ALABAMA FOOTBALL, DODGERS BASEBALL AND TWO NFL GAMES: INSIDE ONE GROUP'S INCREDIBLE SOUTHERN SPORTS TRIP

A collision course for two teams, with a lot on the line.

During the week, questions lingered about whether this game would actually take place with Hurricane Isaias making landfall and then heading on a northern track through the state of Alabama.

University officials had met multiple times in the days and hours leading up to this weekend to discuss contingency plans in case the game needed to either be postponed a few hours, or moved.

All the while, Alabama decided that fans would not be allowed to set up any type of tailgate until after 12 noon local time today in an abundance of caution for the wind and rain that would devour the area.

FIVE IMPORTANT COLLEGE FOOTBALL QUESTIONS THAT WILL BE ANSWERED AFTER THIS WEEKEND'S SLATE

Georgia Bulldogs head coach Kirby Smart tells the students section to calm down during the fourth quarter of an NCAA football game, Saturday, Nov. 1, 2025 at EverBank Stadium in Jacksonville, Florida. (Corey Perrine/Florida Times-Union)

This forced President Donald Trump, who was scheduled to attend the SEC showdown, to back out of traveling to Alabama, with a final decision coming on Friday afternoon. In reality, with everything taking place around Tuscaloosa over a 48-hour period, this turned out to be the most logical decision for all parties involved.

Power trucks sat in the parking lot of the Tuscaloosa mall, while the campus started to slow down on Friday night, with so many unknowns leading up to this day.

On the field tonight, this is about two SEC teams looking to make a statement. Kirby Smart is hoping to exorcise some of the Crimson Tide demons that have followed him during his time as the Bulldogs head coach.

Smart is 2-7 against Alabama during his time in Athens, which is a record he would prefer to start chipping away at. Sure, he's obviously had success against the Tide during the postseason, but there is obviously something different about rolling into Bryant Denny Stadium and beating the school that afforded him the chance to become a head coach.

PAUL FINEBAUM’S PROCLAMATION ABOUT ALABAMA COACH KALEN DEBOER REIGNITES COLLEGE FOOTBALL ‘CULTURE FIT’ DEBATE

To do that, the Dawgs might have to flip the script compared to what some are thinking.

Can quarterback Gunner Stockton beat Alabama through the air?

Sure, but this is also against a team that is starting to find its offensive wings behind Keelon Russell, along with a defense that has clearly found an aggressiveness that we haven’t seen on a consistent basis during DeBoer's tenure in Tuscaloosa.

Alabama Crimson Tide head coach Kalen Deboer looks on against the Georgia Bulldogs during the first quarter in the 2025 SEC Championship at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, Georgia on on Dec. 06, 2025. (Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images)

In reality, these two teams are finding their own identities. For Alabama, last week's dominant win against Mississippi State seems to have instilled a confidence within the fan base.

"I'm not going to compare this type of aggression to the Saban era, but they look as though they're playing pissed off," Edward, from Cullman told OutKick. "I don't know what changed, but it's pretty obvious that Kane Wommack has found a cohesive group.

"Hell, I don't care what it is. But, if we keep this up then who knows where this team could end up this season. We gotta get through the Dawgs, and I really want to see them beat Georgia with a strong defensive performance. I was kind of hoping the rain would at least stick around and allow us to get dirty in the trenches."

The last time Kirby Smart led his team out of the visitors locker room in Tuscaloosa, he stood at the gate bouncing up and down as 'Thunderstruck' played over the stadium loudspeakers.

If he could've, the Georgia head coach looked as though he was ready to throw on pads himself. What we will see tonight are two teams looking to create their own narrative around the 2026 season.

This isn’t about last year, or the teams that came before them.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

But, that doesn’t mean these players don't understand what it means to take the field in this heated rivalry. All week, the college football world has drooled over a well-done Nick Saban documentary, while Kirby Smart smiled and complimented his former boss during a number of interviews.

ESPN College GameDay analyst Nick Saban talks during the show on the lawn of Ayres Hall at the University of Tennessee in Knoxville, Tenn., on Sept. 26, 2026. (Getty Images)

Around Alabama, it wouldn’t be surprising to hear that Kalen DeBoer has heard the tales being told about the guy he replaced.

And while those stories will live on forever, DeBoer is still working to quiet the noise that comes with every decision made regarding his football team.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

What would Saban do? How would Nick handle the game plan? What does the guy who still has an office inside Bryant Denny Stadium really think about his successor?

Tonight, the guy that replaced the legend gets a chance to create a smidge of distance between himself and what many proclaim to be the GOAT of college football coaching.

On the other side, Kirby Smart is hoping to tighten-up his record against the team who employed him as defensive coordinator.

Even though there is obviously more on the line than a regular weekend in the SEC, both Georgia and Alabama are trying to write their own story pertaining to the 2026 season.

That road to the college football playoff continues tonight in Tuscaloosa, with two teams who have grown to truly hate each other, with just a little respect thrown in.

Trey Wallace is the Sr. College Sports Reporter for OutKick.

title: Child among seven killed by Israel in Gaza on ‘ceasefire’ anniversary
excerpt: At least seven people, including an eight-year-old girl, have been killed in Israeli attacks across Gaza, according to medical sources, a year after the United States-backed “ceasefire” came into effe...
body_text:
At least seven people, including an eight-year-old girl, have been killed in Israeli attacks across Gaza, according to medical sources, a year after the United States-backed “ceasefire” came into effect – “in name only”.

Shahd Abdul-Razzaq al-Najjar, 8, was killed on Saturday by an Israeli quadcopter drone in the al-Jawazat area of western Gaza City, according to a source in ambulance and emergencies speaking to Al Jazeera.

In the same part of Gaza City, four people were killed and several injured in a separate Israeli bomb attack near Haider Abdel Shafi roundabout, the city’s al-Shifa Hospital said.

One more Palestinian was killed in an Israeli drone attack in the Tuffah neighbourhood of northeastern Gaza City, the hospital said.

In the southern city of Khan Younis, a woman succumbed to injuries sustained in an Israeli attack earlier on Saturday.

Also on Saturday, the enclave’s Ministry of Health said at least 1,481 Palestinians have been killed and 5,254 injured since the so-called ceasefire came into effect on October 10 last year.

Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza has killed at least 74,370 people and injured 175, 371 since October 7, 2023, the ministry added.

In the past 24 hours, Israeli attacks killed at least nine people and injured 65, it said, adding that one more person succumbed to injuries sustained in previous Israeli aggression.

Al Jazeera’s Tareq Abu Azzoum reported from Gaza on Saturday that the “ceasefire” has only heightened uncertainty in the enclave.

“The rhythm of the genocide has not changed,” he said. “The danger has not gone away completely, and that’s why people believe that it has more consequences, far beyond the immediate loss of life.”

On Friday, more than 100 humanitarian, human rights and civil society organisations said in a joint statement that the ceasefire in Gaza exists only in name.

“The ceasefire exists in name only, with Israeli forces continuing to kill and injure Palestinians daily, and restrictions on aid, equipment and rebuilding materials preventing families from recovering,” the statement said.

In the occupied West Bank, at least 12 Israeli settler pogroms were recorded on Saturday morning, according to the Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission.

Israeli settlers assaulted Palestinian farmers through beatings, spraying them with pepper spray, stealing their property and attacking homes, the Wafa news agency reported. They also detained several Palestinians during the attacks with the help of the Israeli military forces.

In the Ramallah and el-Bireh Governorate, settlers, along with the army, forced farmers to leave their lands and threatened them against returning. Two farmers were beaten and pepper-sprayed, as settlers stole a vehicle and their phones.

title: England international Cole Palmer signs new Chelsea deal until 2034
excerpt:
Chelsea ‌attacking midfielder Cole Palmer has ⁠signed a ⁠contract extension that will keep him at Stamford Bridge until 2034, the ⁠Premier League club announced on Saturday.

The 24-year-old England i...
body_text:
Chelsea ‌attacking midfielder Cole Palmer has ⁠signed a ⁠contract extension that will keep him at Stamford Bridge until 2034, the ⁠Premier League club announced on Saturday.

The 24-year-old England international has become a ⁠key figure since joining Chelsea from Manchester City in 2023, scoring 91 goals in 138 appearances across all competitions.

He was ‌part of the squad that won the Club World Cup in 2025 and the 2024-25 UEFA Conference League.

“Speaking to the owners, to the sporting directors and obviously the manager, they gave me a lot of ⁠confidence so it was ⁠only right to sign,” Palmer said. “Speaking to players as well, everyone has the same ambitions.

“I ⁠feel like we win major trophies here consistently.”

Chelsea have ⁠agreed long-term contracts with several first-team players and emerging talent. Forward Joao Pedro recently signed a deal through 2034, and winger ‌Pedro Neto agreed a six-year contract last month.

Earlier on Friday, Chelsea ⁠manager Xabi ⁠Alonso insisted Palmer ‌remains committed to playing for England after the attacker drew criticism for missing the recent international break due to injury.

Palmer, ⁠left out of England’s World Cup squad this year after a persistent groin injury affected his ⁠form, was called up by Thomas Tuchel for Nations League fixtures against Spain, Czechia and Croatia.

However, Palmer was forced to pull out of the squad due ‌to a recurrence of the issue, with Tuchel saying the midfielder “misses too many opportunities” to play in an England shirt.

Asked about Tuchel’s comments, Alonso told reporters: “The most important thing for Cole is to be fully fit, that he ⁠enjoys his game, that he is ⁠feeling OK.

“Whenever he is not, like in the Brentford game, we could see that he was struggling. He’s committed but he needs ⁠to be fully fit to play. We need him – the club and ⁠the national team,” the Spaniard ⁠added.

“Now he’s fine. He’s been feeling better this week. We use the ‌first two weeks for him to recover. It’s a little bit from the pubalgia (groin injury) he had.”

Chelsea, ‌10th ‌in the Premier League standings, host 17th-placed Bournemouth later on Saturday.

title: Angel Reese reveals 'embarrassing' training camp story after reaching WNBA Finals with Atlanta Dream
excerpt: A'ja Wilson found herself face-to-face with a fan Tuesday night during Game 2 of the WNBA playoffs against the Indiana Fever, and Craig Carton is calling her and the league out over the whole incident...
body_text:
A'ja Wilson found herself face-to-face with a fan Tuesday night during Game 2 of the WNBA playoffs against the Indiana Fever, and Craig Carton is calling her and the league out over the whole incident!

Angel Reese has officially reached the WNBA Finals before Caitlin Clark, and gave fans a peek into the process that got her there after finishing off a three-game sweep of the New York Liberty in the semifinals on Friday, which included a training camp exercise that left her feeling "embarrassed' in front of her new Atlanta Dream teammates.

In the postgame news conference, Reese spoke about a moment in training-camp when Coach Karl Smesko stopped a drill and made her hit two consecutive 3-pointers before her teammates could continue.

Angel Reese #5 of the Atlanta Dream reacts after making a basket during the first quarter of Game 3 of the WNBA Playoffs semifinals against the New York Liberty at Barclays Center on Oct. 9, 2026, in New York City. (Getty Images)

Reese said the exercise left her upset with Smesko and worried about embarrassing herself in front of the team.

"It's really hard for me to not want to rush success, and Karl told me how patient I had to be with it. I remember a very moment in training camp where we were going through drills and he stopped everybody and told me I had to make two in a row in front of everybody," Reese said.

"And you never want to shutdown your teammates, you never want to let your teammates down, and we couldn't resume the drill until I made two in a row, and I was upset with him that day for sure. Because I didn't want to let the team down, I didn't want to feel embarrassed and in how long it coulda took me to make them. But now it's like so easy."

ANGEL REESE SETS TWO WNBA RECORDS WITH HISTORIC REBOUNDING PERFORMANCE

Angel Reese of the Atlanta Dream celebrates a three-point shot during the second half against the Dallas Wings at College Park Center in Arlington, Texas, on May 12, 2026. (Stacy Revere/Getty Images)

Reese is known as a poor shooter, and is often mocked for missing easy shots in games. She has even gotten in on the jokes herself by launching merchandise under the brand "Mebounds" in 2025. The term is a mocking play on "rebounds," referring to the rebounds she collects after missing her own shots.

Later in Friday's postgame news conference, Reese was asked how many shots she needed to make two consecutively.

"My teammates are cheering for me on the sideline, and I was pretty embarrassed," Reese added.

Now, months later, she made two 3-pointers in Atlanta’s 85-83 victory over the New York Liberty, which completed a semifinal sweep and sent the Dream to their first Finals since 2013.

Her recollection addressed an area of her game that has attracted scrutiny throughout her professional career. Reese publicly pushed back against criticism of her missed layups in November 2024, following a rookie season in which she made 39.1% of her shots.

Her shooting numbers since then show progress from that rookie season, with a more modest change during her first year in Atlanta. Reese made 45.1% of her shots this regular season, slightly below the 45.8% she made in her second season with Chicago.

She attempted 3-pointers more frequently with the Dream, but still made fewer than one in five during the regular season. Her 19.3% success rate from beyond the arc was only slightly above last year’s 18.2%.

She has made five of 13 playoff 3-point attempts (38.5%). That represents a stronger stretch across just five games.

LIBERTY MAKE OFFICIAL INQUIRY INTO RESET TIMEOUT DISPUTE AFTER OVERTIME LOSS TO DREAM IN WNBA SEMIFINALS

Angel Reese of the Atlanta Dream reacts after a 3-pointer during the fourth quarter against the Los Angeles Sparks at Gateway Center Arena in College Park, Ga., on July 13, 2026. (Todd Kirkland/Getty Images)

Reese’s overall production grew in Atlanta. She averaged a career-high 16.4 points, again led the WNBA in rebounding and won her first Defensive Player of the Year award. She finished Friday’s clinching victory with 22 points and nine rebounds.

The opportunity followed an April trade that sent Reese from Chicago to Atlanta for two first-round draft picks, with the Dream also receiving a future second-round pick swap. Chicago missed the playoffs in both of her seasons there and finished 10-34 in 2025.

Atlanta already had a franchise-record 30-win season behind it and retained a core that included All-Star guards Allisha Gray and Rhyne Howard and two-time WNBA champion Jordin Canada. Reese joined an established playoff team in Smesko’s second season as coach.

The Dream matched that 30-14 record this year and earned the fourth seed, giving them home-court advantage against Washington in the first round and New York in the semifinals. Sixth-seeded Indiana drew defending champion Las Vegas immediately and lost the deciding game on the road.

The Finals berth came despite Atlanta losing center Brionna Jones to a season-ending leg injury and playing the final two games against New York without Gray, who had a left hand injury.

Clark, who entered the WNBA alongside Reese in 2024, reached the playoffs first, during their rookie season. She missed the entire 2025 postseason with an injury, when Indiana eliminated Atlanta before falling one win short of the Finals against Las Vegas.

This year, Clark averaged a career-high 22.3 points and helped lead the highest-scoring offense in WNBA history alongside Kelsey Mitchell and Aliyah Boston. Indiana finished 28-16 before its first-round elimination.

Reese will now pursue her first WNBA championship, with the Finals scheduled to begin Oct. 17. Atlanta is seeking its first title in franchise history.

title: Hurricane Isaias live updates: warning of ‘spinoff tornadoes’ as hundreds of thousands without power
excerpt:
First Atlantic hurricane of the 2026 season makes landfall in the US

Full story: Hurricane Isaias hammers Gulf coast

We have a statement from the Alabama governor, Kay Ivey:

double quotation markRi...
body_text:
First Atlantic hurricane of the 2026 season makes landfall in the US

Full story: Hurricane Isaias hammers Gulf coast

We have a statement from the Alabama governor, Kay Ivey:

double quotation markRight now, we are worried about strong winds, heavy rain and possible spinoff tornadoes in certain parts of the state. As we approach the weekend and any travel plans, make sure you have reliable information as conditions develop. We often hear in emergency management: Hope for the best. Prepare for the worst. That is the approach we need with this particular storm system. After all, we only want to see one Tide roll this weekend. Y’all be safe, heed local warnings and stay weather aware.”

One person has died in Escambia County, Florida due to the tropical storm, according to the county’s sheriff Chip W. Simmons.

“A tree fell on a house and it unfortunately took the life of a lady,” Simmons said in a video published on social media. “And our thoughts and prayers are obviously with that family.”

This seems to be the first death in Florida resulting from the storm. Earlier this morning, Florida governor Ron DeSantis said during an interview with Fox News he had not yet received any reports of fatalities.

Florida governor Ron DeSantis said during an interview with Fox News on Saturday morning that they had not received any reports of fatalities yet in the state.

DeSantis attributed this to likely heightened preparation and previous experience with other tropical storms and hurricanes.

“We’re a peninsula in the middle of a tropical part of the world – we’ve gotta deal with these things,” DeSantis said.

Florida governor Ron DeSantis said no requests for search and rescue assistance had been received following Isaias, which he described as “cautiously, a good sign”.

double quotation markI think that may be a sign that people heeded the warnings, took proper precautions. We sure would love to say we have not gotten a report of a fatality yet, and we’ll see what happens.

There’s also a lot of hazards post-storm that people should be careful of, but so far we’ve had a lot of assets in place that have not been called on, which is a good sign. I’d rather be over-prepared, and not have to use them, than not have what you need.”

He added that emergency crews have been working overnight to clear roads and bridges, restore power and assess damage.

If you’re just joining us, here are the main developments:

Hurricane Isaias has weakened to a post-tropical cyclone early Saturday, the National Hurricane Center (NHC) said, after it made landfall in Florida and lashed the US Gulf Coast with heavy rain and fierce winds.

The category 2 hurricane hit the coast near Destin, Florida, late Friday, with maximum sustained winds of 105 mph.

The storm is expected to move across Alabama and into the Tennessee Valley, the NHC added, with maximum sustained winds decreased to near 35 mph.

More than 900,000 people have been left without power across the south-east, according to poweroutage.us, with Florida and Alabama among the worst-hit.

The NHC warned heavy rainfall across the south-east increases the risk of flash flooding, with southern Alabama, the Florida Panhandle and south-western Georgia expected to be among the hardest-hit areas, while landslides are also possible in the Southern Appalachians.

Alabama governor Kay Ivey said authorities were worried about “possible spinoff tornadoes” in certain parts of the state.

One significant effect of the stronger El Niño is fewer hurricanes in the Atlantic. In the 30 years to 2020, on average the first hurricane arrived by 11 August, the second by 26 August and the third by 7 September.

Isaias’s October arrival marks a stark contrast from this trend.

At the start of the season, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) predicted a quiet year, anticipating between three and six hurricanes, well below the average of seven. The August forecast cut the expected number to between two and six. Until this year, the latest date for the first Atlantic hurricane was 11 September, in 2002 and 2013.

El Niño is marked by comparatively warm sea surface temperatures in the Pacific and a weakening of the seasonal trade winds. One side-effect is that it increases wind shear – the change in wind speed with height – over the Atlantic. This makes it less likely for tropical storms to evolve into hurricanes, as these require relatively stable air to form over a wide area.

But while things have been mostly quiet on the Atlantic side of the Americas, the eastern Pacific has seen plenty of activity, with 10 hurricanes so far.

We have a statement from the Alabama governor, Kay Ivey:

double quotation markRight now, we are worried about strong winds, heavy rain and possible spinoff tornadoes in certain parts of the state. As we approach the weekend and any travel plans, make sure you have reliable information as conditions develop. We often hear in emergency management: Hope for the best. Prepare for the worst. That is the approach we need with this particular storm system. After all, we only want to see one Tide roll this weekend. Y’all be safe, heed local warnings and stay weather aware.”

Here are some images on the newswires of the hurricane passing through Pensacola, Florida:

As a hurricane approaches a coast, the churning winds force ocean water up on to land; atmospheric pressure from the storm also helps squeeze the water ashore. The shallower the continental shelf, the higher the threat of a dangerous surge. The water may take a couple of days to fully subside.

Water is heavy – about 1,700lb, or 770kg, to a cubic yard (0.76 cubic meters) – and it can move fast in a surge, sweeping people to their deaths, throwing about boats and vehicles, and pulverizing structures. Six inches of fast-moving water is enough to knock over an adult, the National Hurricane Center (NHC) says. Surges become even more dangerous as they coincide with high tide.

Hurricane Katrina in 2005 caused storm surges of over 25ft on the Mississippi coastline. The NHC says many of the 1,500 people killed lost their lives, directly or indirectly, due to the storm surges.

Our data visuals team has been keeping tabs on the path of hurricane Isaias. Here’s where we expect it to hit:

The storm is expected to move across Alabama and into the Tennessee Valley later today and Sunday, the National Hurricane Center (NHC) said in its latest advisory.

“Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher gusts. Slow weakening is forecast today, and Isaias is forecast to dissipate on Sunday,” the center said.

The NHC warned heavy rainfall across the south-east increases the risk of flash flooding, with southern Alabama, the Florida Panhandle and south-western Georgia expected to be among the hardest-hit areas, while landslides are also possible in the Southern Appalachians.

Isaias has left more than 860,000 people without electricity as it moves inland across the south-east.

Here’s the latest breakdown of the worst affected states, according to poweroutage.us:

More than half a million people were without power after hurricane Isaias wreaked havoc on the US Gulf Coast, with Alabama and the Florida Panhandle being hit the hardest by the storm.

The category 2 hurricane made landfall near Destin, Florida, late Friday, with maximum sustained winds of 105 miles per hour. It weakened to a post-tropical cyclone by early morning, with winds of 65 mph, the National Weather Service said.

More than 750,000 people in Florida and Alabama have been left without power, according to poweroutage.us, with outages also reported in Georgia for tens of thousands of customers.

“Things are flying really fast, and I’ve never seen wind this fast before, so it’s intense, it’s scary,” Jonathan Ramos, a 40-year-old government employee, said from his hotel in Pensacola, Florida, where the power went out.

“I don’t recommend people coming down here for fun to do this.”

Isaias intensified into a hurricane on Wednesday night, then becoming the first Atlantic hurricane of the 2026 season.

In the days prior to landfall, storm surge warnings were in effect from the mouth of the Mississippi River to the Suwannee River in Florida. Residents in the affected areas were urged to follow advice from local officials and evacuate if instructed to do so.

Stick with us as we bring you the latest news and updates from hurricane Isaias.

title: 'Cockroach' group leaders among hundreds detained in Delhi protest
excerpt:
Delhi Police has not commented on the detentions

Hundreds of protesters have reportedly been detained in Delhi during the latest demonstration by the Gen-Z led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) over electo...
body_text:
Delhi Police has not commented on the detentions

Hundreds of protesters have reportedly been detained in Delhi during the latest demonstration by the Gen-Z led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) over electoral reforms.

The group said its founder Abhijeet Dipke, who began the movement in May after India's Chief Justice likened some jobless young people to "cockroaches", was detained with other leaders shortly after landing in Delhi.

Tens of thousands of security personnel were deployed and roads barricaded ahead of the demonstration, though the CJP insisted it would go ahead.

Delhi Police has not commented on the detentions, but had refused permission for the protest to take place at Jantar Mantar, a landmark in the Indian capital.

The group - who are not registered as a political party in India - are seeking electoral reforms just months before crucial state elections.

It has also demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of manipulating voters' lists - which the Election Commission has denied.

Under Kumar's leadership, India's election commission has undertaken a mammoth exercise to update electoral rolls nationwide - it said this was a routine exercise to weed out dead, duplicate or ineligible voters.

But in many states, the exercise has been shrouded in controversy, with tens of thousands of people alleging they have been wrongly removed.

The CJP - and opposition parties - accuse Kumar of favouring Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in the way the electoral rolls are being updated.

The Election Commission and the BJP have denied this.

Before arriving in Delhi, the CJP's founder Dipke said: "If you think you can stop us by threatening us with jail or trying to intimidate us with the fear of imprisonment, you are mistaken."

He and and two other leaders, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, were detained on their flight from Mumbai on Saturday.

The group claimed the three men have been taken to an undisclosed location. Delhi Police have not commented.

'Cockroach' leaders say they have been detained ahead of march

Ajinkya Shinde, the CJP's new designated leader while the others are in detention, released a video telling protesters that "if Delhi Police tries to stop you, wherever they stop you will become your Jantar Mantar".

Student activist Neha Bora, who had also been detained by Delhi Police, urged demonstrators to "hold the line".

The large number of protesters expected to descend on Delhi were unable to get anywhere close to Jantar Mantar due to the heavy security presence and road blocks.

Announcements could be heard across the city, asking people to co-operate with the police.

One protester, Sabika Muzaffar, told the BBC she and her mother expected to be detained.

"On the way to the protest site, instead of reciting hymns and verses as we usually do, my mother and I were rote learning our lawyer's number," she said.

She said that showing up to protest was "her way of defending the country and its democracy".

A few minutes after Muzaffar spoke to the BBC she was taken away by police.

Several trains to and from major Delhi stations had been cancelled and dozens of metro stations were closed from Friday night.

Buses packed with detained protesters were seen being driven away from the protest site.

Detained protesters were driven away from the site in police buses

The CJP first emerged as a major protest movement during weeks of demonstrations over the summer demanding education reforms and the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.

The group stemmed from a joke made by Dipke in response to a remark by India's Chief Justice Surya Kant, who had likened jobless youngsters to "cockroaches". He later said the comments were misinterpreted.

Dipke, who previously worked with the opposition Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), had just completed a master's degree at Boston University when he posted a question on X in May: "What if all cockroaches come together?"

The post went viral, and the CJP was born. Momentum built around the movement which tapped into anger over over unemployment, exam paper leaks and government accountability.

In July, Dipke watched from the stage as the five-week-long protest ended in celebration after the resignation of India's education minister.

Meet India's feisty Gen Z protester who is taking on Modi

Lockdown-like scenes at usually bustling central Delhi markets

India's 'cockroach' protesters are back - this time asking poll chief to resign

title: Headmaster detained after BBC investigation into alleged sexual abuse of students
excerpt:
Ex-headmaster Ahmad Imanuddin Sumar, known to students as Abah, has been accused of sexual abuse

A former headmaster of an Islamic boarding school in Indonesia has been named as a suspect in a sexual...
body_text:
Ex-headmaster Ahmad Imanuddin Sumar, known to students as Abah, has been accused of sexual abuse

A former headmaster of an Islamic boarding school in Indonesia has been named as a suspect in a sexual abuse investigation and detained by police, following a BBC Eye report.

Ahmad Imanuddin Sumar, known to students as Abah, led the Abul Barokat boarding school on the island of Lombok.

Police reopened the case after the BBC World Service revealed accusations of sexual abuse against him, and documented how former students had gathered evidence in an effort to bring the allegations to the authorities.

The story sparked public outrage and led to 12 more former students giving testimony to police.

Warning: This story contains details of sexual assault

Two ex-students expose sexual abuse by teachers at Islamic boarding schools in Indonesia

Outside the UK, you can watch Catching My Teacher on YouTube, external.

Central to the BBC Eye investigation were former students Ziadatur Rahmah, known as Zia, and Sukma Rohana Fajar.

They launched their own investigation after Zia told a former classmate, Yusron Azzahidi, that the headteacher had sexually assaulted her when she was 17. The pair had been star pupils at the school.

By the time Zia confided in Yusron, she was studying in Cairo, Egypt, while he was in Jakarta.

Yusron suggested they gather evidence to support Zia's allegation. Speaking to former classmates, they spoke to Sukma, who alleges that Abah attempted to rape her at the school.

Yusron compiled a seven-page document detailing the allegations, and they gave it to representatives of Nahdlatul Wathan Diniyah Islamiyah (NWDI), the organisation that ran the school.

Thinking the school would support them, the students say that instead, they were pressured to withdraw their accusations.

In a secretly recorded phone call, Abah pleaded with Yusron to protect him and his reputation.

"Cover the shame of your teacher. Everyone makes mistakes, my child," Abah said.

Abah also contacted Zia, who secretly recorded their conversation and shared it with the BBC.

In the recording, Abah is heard apologising, but pleads with her to remain silent.

Following the BBC investigation, Abah held a news conference where he denied all the allegations. He did not deny that the voice heard in the recorded calls was his, but said the recordings were not confessions.

Sukma told the BBC she had been forced to sign a document saying her allegations were lies. She later secretly recorded a conversation with Abah's wife, known to students as Umi. In the recording, Umi tells Sukma that the document was intended to protect "her good name".

The former students eventually resumed their efforts to seek justice, with support from lawyer Joko Jumadi, who has experience in similar cases.

Watch: BBC tracks down abusive teacher secretly released early

The day after the BBC investigation was published, parents arrived at the school to collect their children, with some travelling from other islands.

One mother said she had begun crying when she heard the news, thinking about her daughter.

"I'm moving her right now," she said. "I absolutely want my child to leave this school."

Yusron said he and Zia, who recently got married, were overwhelmed by the response from former students.

"It was beyond what we expected," he said. "So many people contacted us - on Instagram, WhatsApp. They contacted me and Zia directly, and lots of them were saying, 'I'm a victim too'."

Police interviewed Zia and Sukma, along with the 12 other former students who came forward with allegations of abuse.

"They thought they were the only ones - and it's been really shocking for them to learn, like I did, that they weren't alone," Zia said.

Sukma said she felt relieved and grateful that the allegations are now being taken seriously.

"It's not about revenge. It's more the acknowledgement that what he did was wrong. I'm waiting for the day when he admits that himself," she told the BBC.

Abah has resigned from the school and has said he will respect the legal process.

The BBC contacted Abah and his wife during its original investigation, but they did not respond at the time.

NWDI denied trying to cover up the allegations and said it was investigating them internally. It said it had a duty to protect the organisation from being tarnished by the alleged actions of individuals.

In the wake of the BBC investigation, NWDI vowed to ensure such abuse never happened again and said it would safeguard the rights of students who came forward.
